fixes.explanation: Yes, baker, you got it. The text says it is "…impossible for God to lie…" (Hebrews 6:18). God made a promise to Abraham and guaranteed it with an oath (Hebrews 6:13, 17). Those are the two unchangeable things. That's a solid base to stand on.
Close, but angels aren't who He swore by. The text says He "…had no one greater to swear by…" and angels are not greater than God. So "…He swore by Himself…" (Hebrews 6:13).
Yes, baker! God said, "I will surely bless you and multiply your descendants." (Hebrews 6:14). Blessing and a whole lot of family. I think Abraham was going to need a bigger dinner table.
Not hidden, friend. The oath was meant to make the unchanging nature of His purpose "very clear" (Hebrews 6:17). Hiding is the opposite of what He was doing. The word is "unchanging."

That's right, baker. The text says that by these two unchangeable things, "…we who have fled to take hold of the hope set before us may be strongly encouraged." (Hebrews 6:18). Strong encouragement is what those two things give.
Moses, Israel's leader (Exodus 3:10), is a big name, friend, but he's not the one here. The text says "…Jesus our forerunner has entered on our behalf." (Hebrews 6:20). Jesus went in ahead of us.
David, Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3), is a great pick, baker, but he's not who the writer means. The text says "…Jesus our forerunner has entered on our behalf." (Hebrews 6:20). Jesus went in first.
